title: Dwarf galaxy Pisces B
caption: The dwarf galaxy Pisces B, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Pisces B, [SCB2015] GALFA-Dw2 · constellation Pisces · about 30 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Hubble image archive. No published rating.

story: This Hubble picture shows the galaxy Pisces B. Below and to the left of center sits a bright object with spikes of light radiating from it. That object is not part of Pisces B but a foreground star in our own Milky Way. Several distant galaxies also appear in the background.
Pisces B is a dwarf galaxy, a small galaxy with far fewer stars than a large spiral like the Milky Way. It lies about 30 million light-years away.

The spikes around the bright star are diffraction spikes. They are not real features of the star. They appear because of the way a telescope's structure bends incoming light, and they tend to show up around bright point sources such as nearby stars. The fainter background galaxies lie far beyond Pisces B.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (1.35 x 1.35 arcminutes) and distance (30 million light years), the frame spans roughly 12,000 × 12,000 light-years. Its light set out about 30 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed Pisces B in visible and near-infrared light. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared filter records light the eye cannot see, and a dwarf galaxy this distant is far too faint to see without a telescope.

explore: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took the picture through two filters, one in visible light and one in the near-infrared. The object list also names Pisces B by its catalog designation, [SCB2015] GALFA-Dw2.
alt: A faint dwarf galaxy with a bright foreground star showing diffraction spikes below left of center and small distant galaxies in the background.
